newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen higher, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen higher, feeders steady to up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open 0.200 to 0.400 cent per lb higher while feeders were called steady to 0.200 higher, livestock analysts said.

The stronger tone to fed cattle markets as packers raised prices to obtain fed cattle Wednesday and further strength in boxed beef values were seen as supporting influences. However, action in pork pits linked to news of a foot and mouth disease outbreak in Taiwan hogs may influence futures, analysts said.
Any sharp upward price move in pork will spark short covering in cattle pits, they said.

Feeder cattle were expected to show a firmer tone on recent strength in cash feeder cattle prices. A stronger tone to fed cattle should keep the market supported despite higher early indications on corn futures, they said.
Feeders will also follow other meat pits if the Taiwan pork news sparks a short covering rally, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.05 at $68.45 per cwt.
